s.d: a diacritical mark (two dots) placed over a vowel to indicate a change in sound in some languages

s.d: The umlaut process (as above) that occurred historically in Germanic languages whereby back vowels became front vowels when followed by syllable containing a front vocoid (e.g. Germanic lūsiz > Old English lȳs(i) > Modern English lice).
A vowel so assimilated.

(informal) Synonym of diaeresis.
